GREMLINS fits block models to **multipartite networks**: collections of simple and bipartite networks
involving common groups of nodes (the functional groups), possibly with different types of weights
and with missing values. The model and its inference are described in
Bar-Hen, Barbillon and Donnet (2022), *Block models for generalized multipartite networks: Applications
in ecology and ethnobiology*, Statistical Modelling, 22(4), 273–296,
[doi:10.1177/1471082X20963254](https://doi.org/10.1177/1471082X20963254).

::: {.callout-important}
## Please use GREMLINS through the package `sbm`

GREMLINS is the inference engine of the package [`sbm`](https://CRAN.R-project.org/package=sbm).
**We recommend not to use GREMLINS directly, but the function `estimateMultipartiteSBM()` of `sbm`**,
which implements the same model and the same algorithm, with a simpler interface (shared with simple,
bipartite and multiplex networks), plot functions and examples. GREMLINS is maintained as a back-end of `sbm`.
:::

## Documentation

The documentation of multipartite block models is in the vignettes of `sbm`:

- *Stochastic Block Models for Multipartite networks: principle*: the model, its inference and an illustration
  on simulated data (selection of the numbers of blocks, fixed numbers of blocks, initial clustering,
  missing data and prediction, parallel computing),
  `vignette("MultipartiteNetwork_principle", package = "sbm")`;
- *Multipartite Stochastic Block Models*: the analysis of a mutualistic ecological network,
  `vignette("Multipartite_EcologicalNetwork", package = "sbm")`.

## From GREMLINS to sbm

| GREMLINS                         | `sbm`                                                                    |
|----------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| `defineNetwork()`                | `defineSBM()`                                                            |
| `rMBM()`                         | `sampleMultipartiteSBM()`                                                |
| `multipartiteBM()`               | `estimateMultipartiteSBM()`                                              |
| `multipartiteBMFixedModel()`     | `estimateMultipartiteSBM()` with equal bounds in `nbBlocksRange`         |
| options `v_Kmin`, `v_Kmax`       | `estimOptions$nbBlocksRange`                                             |
| options `initBM`, `classifInit`  | `estimOptions$initBM`, `estimOptions$classifInit`                        |
| `$fittedModel` (`keep = TRUE`)   | `$storedModels`, `$setModel()`                                           |
| `extractClustersMBM()`           | `$memberships`                                                           |
| `predictMBM()`                   | `predict()`                                                              |
| (none)                           | `plot()`, `plotMyMultipartiteMatrix()`                                   |

For instance, the analysis of the ecological network `MPEcoNetwork` (also available in `sbm` as
`multipartiteEcologicalNetwork`) reads, with GREMLINS:

```{r gremlins, eval = FALSE}
library(GREMLINS)
data(MPEcoNetwork)
PlantFlovis <- defineNetwork(MPEcoNetwork$Inc_plant_flovis, "inc", "Plants", "Flovis")
PlantAnt    <- defineNetwork(MPEcoNetwork$Inc_plant_ant,    "inc", "Plants", "Ants")
PlantBird   <- defineNetwork(MPEcoNetwork$Inc_plant_bird,   "inc", "Plants", "Birds")
res <- multipartiteBM(list(PlantFlovis, PlantAnt, PlantBird),
                      v_distrib = c("bernoulli", "bernoulli", "bernoulli"),
                      namesFG = c("Plants", "Flovis", "Ants", "Birds"))
res$fittedModel[[1]]$paramEstim$v_K
```

and with `sbm`:

```{r sbm, eval = FALSE}
library(sbm)
data(multipartiteEcologicalNetwork)
Net <- multipartiteEcologicalNetwork
PlantFlovis <- defineSBM(Net$Inc_plant_flovis, "bernoulli", "bipartite", dimLabels = c("Plants", "Flovis"))
PlantAnt    <- defineSBM(Net$Inc_plant_ant,    "bernoulli", "bipartite", dimLabels = c("Plants", "Ants"))
PlantBird   <- defineSBM(Net$Inc_plant_bird,   "bernoulli", "bipartite", dimLabels = c("Plants", "Birds"))
myMSBM <- estimateMultipartiteSBM(list(PlantFlovis, PlantAnt, PlantBird))
myMSBM$nbBlocks
plot(myMSBM)
```
